As artificial intelligence and cloud applications grow, the large data centers powering them are facing a major resource crisis. The thousands of computer servers in these facilities produce massive amounts of heat and require huge volumes of water to stay cool.

Many data centers use evaporative cooling towers. This process turns freshwater into water vapor, removing it permanently from local drinking water supplies. The leftover wastewater contains high concentrations of salt and treatment chemicals, which can strain local sewer systems and pollute nearby rivers.

While tech companies highlight job creation and local tax revenue, residents often face higher utility rates and strict water limits. Better alternatives do exist to protect local water supplies:

Closed-loop systems: Cooling setups that reuse and recirculate the same water continuously.

Recycled wastewater: Using treated non-potable water instead of clean drinking water.
